questions.stem: The key difference between IDS and IPS is:

choices.B: IDS monitors and alerts; IPS actively blocks detected threats inline

questions.explanation: An IDS passively monitors and generates alerts. An IPS is deployed inline and actively blocks detected threats in real time.

questions.stem: A SIEM correlates logs from multiple sources to:

choices.A: Detect threats invisible to individual components by identifying multi-stage attack patterns

questions.explanation: A SIEM collects logs across the environment and correlates events across time and systems to surface attack chains.

choices.C: SQL injection matching a rule pattern
choices.D: Zero-day attacks with no existing signature

questions.explanation: Signature-based detection requires a matching pattern. Novel zero-day threats have no signature and bypass this detection entirely.

choices.A: A real attack that goes undetected
choices.B: A correctly identified and blocked attack
choices.C: An alert generated for legitimate non-malicious activity
choices.D: A system reporting its own vulnerability

questions.explanation: A false positive incorrectly flags benign activity as malicious, wasting analyst time and contributing to alert fatigue.

questions.stem: The MOST dangerous IDS outcome is:
questions.explanation: A false negative, a real attack that goes undetected, is most dangerous because the attack proceeds with no defensive response.

choices.A: Matching events against known attack signatures
choices.B: Checking file hashes against a known-good database
choices.C: Comparing activity against a learned baseline and flagging statistical deviations

questions.explanation: Anomaly-based detection establishes a baseline of normal behaviour and alerts on significant deviations, enabling detection of novel threats.

questions.stem: Alert fatigue in a SOC results from:

choices.B: Encrypted traffic that cannot be inspected
choices.C: Too many low-quality or false-positive alerts causing analysts to dismiss real threats

questions.explanation: Alert fatigue from excessive poor-quality alerts causes analysts to stop investigating carefully, increasing the risk of missing real attacks.

questions.stem: SIEM correlation rules detect multi-stage attacks by:

choices.A: Linking related events across multiple systems and time periods into coherent attack narratives
choices.B: Blocking individual suspicious events in real time
choices.C: Comparing all traffic against threat intelligence feeds

questions.explanation: Correlation rules connect events across systems, e.g., port scan → login failure → new admin account, revealing attack chains.

choices.A: Only monitors traffic addressed to its own IP
choices.D: Receives copies of all traffic on the segment without being in the traffic path

questions.explanation: Promiscuous mode enables the NIC to receive all frames on the segment, allowing passive monitoring of all traffic.

choices.C: Forensic investigation of attacks discovered weeks or months after initial compromise
choices.D: Automatic expiry of stale firewall rules

questions.explanation: Many breaches are discovered long after initial compromise. Adequate retention ensures historical evidence exists for full forensic reconstruction.
